c: PIED-P30 (LR 5): unsupported. The only figure found is from an uncontrolled adult foot-and-ankle clinic series, in which subtalar motion was decreased in 23 of 32 feet (72%) with coalition. Without a comparison group, specificity and LRs cannot be derived. Rigid flatfoot with minimal subtalar motion also occurs without coalition, as shown in idiopathic rigid and peroneal spastic flatfoot series. Only one of the six codes (PIED-P35) has a published accuracy study, and one more (PIED-P31) has indirect data from which accuracy can be calculated; the other four have no data. No meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy and no primary-care or emergency cohort turned up for any of the four diagnoses. PIED-P31 (LR+ 6, LR− 0.3): only indirect data, which do not fit the intended use. In the Kamel study every participant already had an accessory navicular, and the comparison is edematous versus non-edematous ossicles. The specificity therefore says nothing about separating accessory navicular from other causes of medial midfoot pain. Navicular bone stress injury, for example, produces navicular tenderness in 96% of adolescent cases.

PIED-P32 (LR+ 6, LR− 0.3): no data. One specialist orthopedic hospital study recorded navicular tuberosity tenderness in 110 patients, but it tested MRI edema against tenderness (the reverse direction), and the abstract gives no counts. The full text may contain a 2×2 table that could be inverted.
